claim: The security fallback for types that are not explicitly approved as hash-collision resistant now returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default instead of throwing. An untrusted payload can therefore populate a hash-based collection using a custom key type with colliding or attacker-controlled hashes, regressing the stated hash-collision protection. This runtime security change is also unrelated to the requested source-generation feature.

receipt_plan.detail: Add or run a MessagePack runtime security test that deserializes an untrusted hash-based collection whose key type is not on the hash-resistant whitelist and whose equality comparer produces colliding hashes. The base behavior should throw TypeAccessException at this fallback; the head behavior proceeds with EqualityComparer<T>.Default, demonstrating the regression.

claim: MessagePack attributes already present on the referenced data type are not honored. With no surrogate, the collector unconditionally calls CreateContractlessMembers and never inspects MessagePackObjectAttribute, KeyAttribute, or IgnoreMemberAttribute on T. Thus a [MessagePackObject] type with integer keys and ignored members is emitted as a name-keyed contractless map including those ignored members, contrary to the acceptance criteria.

claim: The fallback for key types without an explicitly registered hash-resistant comparer now returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default instead of throwing. Untrusted hash-based collection deserialization consequently accepts arbitrary custom key types with potentially collision-prone hashes, enabling the hash-collision denial-of-service attack that this guard and its adjacent comment exist to prevent.

receipt_plan.detail: Expose MessagePackSecurity.GetHashCollisionResistantEqualityComparer<T> through a test subclass and invoke it for a non-whitelisted custom key type, or deserialize a hash-based collection with that key type using MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData. The existing security contract requires TypeAccessException; head returns/uses the default equality comparer instead.

claim: MessagePack attributes on T are not honoured: when no surrogate is supplied, the collector always builds a contractless string-key model, ignoring [MessagePackObject], [Key], and [IgnoreMember] on T. A generated formatter for an attributed type therefore uses different member membership and wire keys instead of its declared MessagePack contract.

receipt_plan.detail: Define ProjectA.MyType as [MessagePackObject] public class MyType { [Key(0)] public int A { get; set; } [Key(1)] public string B { get; set; } [IgnoreMember] public int Ignored { get; set; } }. claim: The fallback for key types without a known hash-resistant comparer now returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default instead of throwing. Consequently, MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData permits hash-based collections with unapproved key types and loses its hash-collision denial-of-service protection; an attacker can supply colliding keys to force pathological dictionary lookups.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a regression test that deserializes a Dictionary or HashSet whose key element type has no whitelisted collision-resistant comparer using options.WithSecurity(MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData). The test should expect TypeAccessException (the prior secure behavior); on this change deserialization instead reaches EqualityComparer<T>.Default. A key type with a constant GetHashCode can additionally demonstrate that attacker-controlled collisions are accepted.

claim: The new collector always selects surrogate mode or collects all public read-write members contractlessly; it never checks T for [MessagePackObject]/[DataContract] or reads its [Key]/[IgnoreMember] annotations. Consequently, an attributed T does not have its declared keys and membership honoured, violating an explicit acceptance criterion.
